subject.title: Reply-session init conflict is silently dropped on Slack/webchat/heartbeat inbound, though Telegram already treats it as retryable

question: Should this issue be resolved by the shared fenced reply-session self-heal in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920, or should maintainers require explicit WebChat and heartbeat retry parity before treating the bug as fixed?
rationale: Current source supports both a shared root-cause fix and remaining surface-level terminalization paths; choosing the recovery layer affects session lifecycle ownership and channel retry boundaries.

options.title: Review Shared Self-Heal First
options.body: Treat the open shared self-heal PR as the primary fix path, then verify WebChat and heartbeat behavior after it lands.

options.title: Require Surface Retry Parity
options.body: Keep the shared PR separate and require explicit WebChat and heartbeat retry or spool handling before this issue can close.

options.title: Ask For Live Surface Proof
options.body: Request a current-main WebChat or heartbeat timing reproduction before choosing between shared recovery and surface retries.

recommendation.title: Review Shared Self-Heal First
recommendation.body: Treat the open shared self-heal PR as the primary fix path, then verify WebChat and heartbeat behavior after it lands.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman has the strongest recent history on the session accessor and gateway transcript boundary where this owner-layer choice sits.
